core_classification.analysis: Mejer’s “Jeg har elsket Dem” (“I have loved You”) is primarily an explicit avowal presented as true, elaborated by a claimed lifelong duration and suffering. The broader turn carries weak undertaking-like pressure because he refuses to promise mere friendship and asks leave to relate to Constance as he feels compelled to, but the highlighted clause does not itself clearly institute a commitment. Its emotional delivery remains an impassioned assertion rather than an independently evidenced reflex-like discharge.
core_classification.ambiguity: The surrounding declaration of devotion gives limited support to P, but it is unclear whether Mejer is undertaking anything beyond avowing an enduring state.

utterance_status.description: Mejer directly addresses Constance and avows that he has loved her throughout his life, beginning when he first saw her.

contextual_interpretation: The avowal answers Constance’s request that they remain only friends. Mejer refuses to predetermine his conduct, presents his love and suffering as longstanding, and asks permission to be as he “can and must.” Constance’s anxiety, her marriage, and his subsequent “I am Yours” make the declaration relationally consequential and pressuring, but they do not alter its dominant truth-conditional force. His melancholy and passionate delivery supply intensity, not independent expressive/reflexive force.

evidence.quotation_or_description: “Jeg har elsket Dem hele mit Liv, fra den første Tid jeg saa Dem” (“I have loved You all my life, from the first time I saw You”).
evidence.supports: The explicit first-person claim, with duration and onset specified, strongly supports truth-conditional avowal.

evidence.quotation_or_description: Constance asks Mejer to promise that they will be “Venner, kun Venner”; he replies that he cannot decide beforehand how he will be toward her.
evidence.supports: The declaration occurs as a reason for rejecting a merely friendly relational constraint, giving weak secondary support to performative or undertaking force.

evidence.quotation_or_description: The avowal continues: “jeg har lidt i en Grad, saa De aner det ikke. Giv mig Lov til at være, som jeg kan og maa” (“I have suffered to a degree You cannot imagine. Give me leave to be as I can and must”).
evidence.supports: His suffering reinforces the presented emotional state, while the request for permission adds relational pressure without turning the love clause itself into a clear commitment.

evidence.quotation_or_description: The narration gives his voice a melancholy note, and he later cries passionately, “Jeg er Deres, De ejer mig” (“I am Yours; You possess me”).
evidence.supports: The scene is emotionally intense and includes adjacent commitment-like language, but there is no evidence that “Jeg har elsket Dem” is blurted or functions as reflex-like affective discharge.

ontology_assessment.diagnosis: T naturally captures the central avowal, with slight P support from its role in resisting a friends-only arrangement. E is unnecessary because the emotional delivery can be represented contextually without positing reflexive core force, and no residual aspect requires O.
